defects_found.description: Stale summary: states 'Final decision count: 184' and describes Lev.21 as ending in a 'four-way layout' with 21:5-8 kept merged (new sibling M8-Lev-186 for 21:9 only). A later revision round (after this section was written) further split 21:5-8 into M8-Lev-127 (Lev.21.5-7) and a new M8-Lev-189 (Lev.21.8), per M8-Lev-127's own boss_ruling.reasoning ('Revision round: narrowed to 21:5-7; the boss differentiator for a 5-8 cap was overruled by the peer on verified grammar') and M8-Lev-189's fresh-review packet. The live artifact set (book_chunks/Lev/chunks.jsonl, reviews/Lev/review_packets.jsonl) is internally consistent at 185 active decisions (ids 1-189 minus retired 10/63/75/94), confirmed by hash integrity and the production validator. This is a documentation lag in the book-writer's own non-authorizing strategy note, not a defect in any frozen candidate row: the other post_adjudication_outcome tallies in the same section (7/7 holds sustained = 6 overruled + 1 insufficient_evidence_marker_only) still match the live data exactly.

13 of 20 peer_crosscheck_history entries (the archived round-1/pre-revision peer crosscheck for decisions that later went through a challenge-and-revision cycle) have entirely blank assessment/disputed_claim_ids/supported_claim_ids/evidence_refs fields, carrying only reviewer_attempt_id/role/model_id/effort. Full reviewer identity and provenance is preserved via routing_record, and each such decision's current (top-level) peer_crosscheck is fully substantive, so no boundary decision is undermined. But a reader inspecting peer_crosscheck_history in isolation would see apparently empty review activity rather than a clear note that this round's peer pass was superseded/deferred. Does not violate the mechanical response-parity contract (validate_book_review_coverage.py passes cleanly).

defects_found.description: 7 packets carry boss_ruling.reasoning = 'Ruled per challenge above.' although that packet's own primary_reviews contain zero challenges. In each case the driving challenge was filed against a sibling decision in the same merge or boundary-shift pair (e.g. M8-Lev-062 inherits the outcome of OL-M8-Lev-063-1, filed on the now-superseded M8-Lev-063; M8-Lev-041 inherits the outcome of OL-M8-Lev-040-1, filed on sibling M8-Lev-040). This is traceable via peer_crosscheck_history cross-references or reviews/Lev/superseded_decisions.jsonl and is not a response-parity violation, but reading any one of these 7 packets in isolation, the phrase 'ruled per challenge above' has no local referent.
